title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is the 1986 manuscript 'Réseaux via découpages'. It belongs to Grothendieck's attempt to axiomatize the 'tame topology' (topologie modérée) programme of Esquisse d'un programme §5–6. The approach does not use point-set topology. Instead it works with an abstract lattice M ('réseau') of 'tame' parts. M carries a closure operator X ↦ X̄ and a notion of 'médiant' (mediating) pairs, and from these it defines open and closed elements. The model case is M = Mod(L): the Boolean lattice of tame subsets of a basic object L. For A ∈ M there is an induced structure M_A. The previous page checked that it is again of the right kind, with induced closure X̄^{M_A} = X̄^M ∧ A.

Connectedness. Also on the previous page, M is called connected if every element that is both closed and open is 0 or 1.

This page (first paragraph). The clopen elements should form a Boolean subalgebra. If that Boolean algebra is finite, the connected components are its atoms: the minimal nonzero clopen elements. Grothendieck adds the convention 0 ≠ 1, i.e. M is not reduced to a point; otherwise one has a degenerate 'empty' structure. This is standard: a finite Boolean algebra is the free join of its atoms, so 1 = ∨ atoms, disjointly, and each atom is connected in the induced structure.

This page (worked example). Take M = Mod(L) and A ∈ M, where A is a thinned (or tame) part of a 'transversal'. Write A = X_Φ with Φ a flag-type datum in Drap*(...), so that A = ∪ T_i, a disjoint union of 'positions transversales' T_i. Claim: the connected components of A are exactly the T_i.

Proof strategy:
- A = ∨ T_i in M and T_i ∧ T_j = ∅ for i ≠ j.
- So it suffices to show (a) each T_i is clopen in A, and (b) each T_i is connected, i.e. it cannot be split into two disjoint nonempty closed parts.

Next page. (a) is reduced to closedness: cl(T_i) ∩ A = T_i. This uses that the tame closure of a transversal position is the associated closed position. For (b) he uses (M_L)_T = M_T to reduce to T = L. Every tame subset is then a union of positions, and a clopen one must be ∅ or L.

Purpose. The page sets up π_0 (connected components) for the abstract tame-lattice formalism and checks it on the basic stratified model.
errors: Clopen elements forming a Boolean algebra is stated only as an expectation ('on s'attend'). Its proof depends on how 'ouvert' and the médiant condition are defined in the abstract réseau, and is not given here.

The description of components as minimal nonzero clopens needs the clopen Boolean algebra to be finite (or at least atomic). Grothendieck flags this himself; nothing on this page guarantees finiteness for general M.

Claim (a) that each T_i is closed in A relies on A being a suitably 'thinned' union of transversal positions. In a general stratification the closure of one stratum meets others, so strata are not components. The page leaves this hypothesis implicit; on the next page it is called 'immédiat'.

ideas.what: Connectedness of an abstract lattice with closure operator, defined by the absence of nontrivial clopen elements; components as atoms of the Boolean algebra of clopens.
ideas.modern_name: Connectedness in closure algebras / Boolean algebra of clopens (Stone duality); definable connectedness
ideas.usually_credited_to: McKinsey–Tarski (closure algebras, 1944); Stone (1936); for tame sets, van den Dries and Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (o-minimal definable connectedness, 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (1984), without this formalism

ideas.what: Components of a tame set that is a disjoint union of (thinned) transversal positions are exactly those positions.
ideas.modern_name: Cells/strata as definably connected components; finiteness of definably connected components in o-minimal structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn; van den Dries, 'Tame topology and o-minimal structures' (1998)

ideas.what: Lattice-theoretic ('réseau') axiomatization of tame topology via a Boolean lattice Mod(L) of tame parts with closure and a médiant relation, with induced structures M_A.
ideas.modern_name: Lattice/closure-algebra approach to o-minimal or tame geometry; compare the o-minimal spectrum as the Stone/spectral space of the lattice of definable sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pillay (o-minimal spectrum, 1988); Coste–Roy (real spectrum); Edmundo–Prelli (o-minimal sites)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's abstract réseau M = Mod(L), with closure and induced substructures M_A, is essentially the Boolean lattice of definable sets with topological closure. The o-minimal spectrum and the o-minimal site (Pillay; Edmundo–Jones–Peatfield; Edmundo–Prelli) are built from the same lattice. His notes develop π_0 and related notions purely lattice-theoretically and independently of model theory. The link between these 1986 notes and the later o-minimal-site literature is not recorded.
missed.quote: Reprenons M = Mod(L), et M_A si A ∈ M = Mod(L)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical precedent for the 'tame topology as a site or lattice' viewpoint. This is mainly of historical rather than technical interest, since the result on this page is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains elementary lattice-theoretic definitions of connectedness and a straightforward example in the stratified model. Its only interest is as part of Grothendieck's unpublished, independent axiomatization of tame topology; the mathematics itself is routine.

'sinon on a [-une-] surtout une structure "vide"' likely reads 'sinon on a [-une-] surtout une structure "vide"', with 'surtout' uncertain; possibly just 'une structure "vide"'.
'les petits morceaux composants $T_i$' should more plausibly read 'les positions [transversales] composant $T_i$' (handwriting 'pos.trans...')
'En effet, on a bien sûr' appears in the image as 'En M_A, on a bien sûr' (or 'En effet' with uncertain reading).
'$= \bigcup T_i$' is written beneath '$X_\Phi$', i.e. $A = X_\Phi = \bigcup T_i$; the 'Trod L' argument of Drap* is uncertain.
